_doc: DERIVED. The atlas's drawn territories at lod2, converted from the artwork's pixel space to lon/lat by tools/build-political-overlay.mjs through the seeded inverse in tools/lib/georef.mjs. Regenerate rather than hand-edit. These are the borders as DRAWN, placed honestly, not re-fitted to the real shoreline: where they disagree with the coastline they disagree visibly, and that disagreement is information. The re-fit is a separate decision recorded in docs/changes/map-timeline/coastline-precision-roadmap.md.

_arctic.why: NOT DRAWN by owner decision, 2026-08-03: no faction territory in Greenland or the high Arctic. The cut is made in the artwork's own pixel space rather than in latitude, because the far north is where the transform is least trustworthy and cutting on its output would mean deciding what to remove using the numbers that are wrong.

_dropped.why: The policy, which currently drops nothing: where the model has no answer on the branch an outline is walked, that territory is ABSENT rather than placed by another root, which would draw it thousands of kilometres away while looking entirely plausible. A missing territory is visible; a confidently misplaced one is not. This listed two territories while the bare quadratic shipped, because its surface folded above about 63N and the walk ran out; the blend adopted on 2026-08-03 has an answer everywhere the artwork draws, so both are back. The rule stays because the reason for it does.

_fitted.why: Clipped to the shipped 1:10m coastline so no faction claims open ocean, then the land the clip orphaned was shared out to the nearest surviving territory by a Voronoi partition of their own boundaries. The artwork's shore is a stylised line rather than a tracing, so clipping alone would have left displaced coastal territories as slivers and the real land beneath them unowned. Regenerate with tools/fit-political-to-land.py; do not hand-edit.
